2363added
2364added-- ### While Loops
2365added
2366added-- The Hoare rule for `while` loops is based on the idea of a *command
2367added-- invariant* (or just *invariant*): an assertion whose truth is guaranteed
2368added-- after executing a command, assuming it is true before.
2369added
2370added-- That is, an assertion `P` is a command invariant of `c` if
2371added
2372added-- {{P}} c {{P}}
2373added
2374added-- holds. Note that the command invariant might temporarily become false in
2375added-- the middle of executing `c`, but by the end of `c` it must be restored.
2376added
2377added-- As a first attempt at a `while` rule, we could try:
2378added
2379added-- {{P}} c {{P}}
2380added-- ---------------------------
2381added-- {{P} while b do c end {{P}}
2382added
2383added-- This rule is valid: if `P` is a command invariant of `c`, as the premise
2384added-- requires, then, no matter how many times the loop body executes, `P` is
2385added-- going to be true when the loop finally finishes.
2386added
2387added-- But the rule also omits two crucial pieces of information. First, the loop
2388added-- terminates when `b` becomes false. So we can strengthen the postcondition
2389added-- in the conclusion:
2390added
2391added-- {{P}} c {{P}}
2392added-- ---------------------------------
2393added-- {{P}} while b do c end {{P ∧ ¬b}}
2394added
2395added-- Second, the loop body will be executed only if `b` is true. So we can also
2396added-- strengthen the precondition in the premise:
2397added
2398added-- {{P ∧ b}} c {{P}}
2399added-- --------------------------------- (hoare_while)
2400added-- {{P}} while b do c end {{P ∧ ¬b}}
2401added
2402added-- That is the Hoare `while` rule. Note how it combines aspects of `skip` and
2403added-- conditionals:
2404added
2405added-- - If the loop body executes zero times, the rule is like `skip` in that the
2406added-- precondition survives to become (part of) the postcondition.
2407added
2408added-- - Like a conditional, we can assume guard `b` holds on entry to the
2409added-- subcommand.
2410added
2411added-- Note to developers:
2412added-- HIDE: The big comment will not display nicely. But I guess it's
2413added-- folded...
2414added
2415addedtheorem hoare_while (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
2416added (hhoare : {{P ∧ b}} ~c {{P}}) :
2417added {{P}} while (~b) { ~c } {{P ∧ ¬b}} := by
2418added intro st st' heval hP
2419added /- We proceed by induction on `heval`, because, in the "keep
2420added looping" case, its hypotheses talk about the whole loop instead
2421added of just `c`. The auxiliary statement `key` generalizes over an
2422added arbitrary command, together with an equation remembering that the
2423added command is the original loop; otherwise, that information would
2424added be lost in the induction. The cases for commands other than
2425added `while` are dismissed because their equations are contradictory. -/
2426added have key : ∀ (cmd : Com) (s s' : State), (s =[ cmd ]=> s') →
2427added cmd = (imp { while (~b) { ~c } }) → P s →
2428added P s' ∧ ¬ bassertion b s' := by
2429added intro cmd s s' hev
2430added induction hev with
2431added | whileFalse b0 s0 c0 hb =>
2432added intro heq hp
2433added injection heq with e1 _
2434added subst e1
2435added exact ⟨hp, bexp_eval_false _ _ hb⟩
2436added | whileTrue s0 s0' s0'' b0 c0 hb hc hloop ih1 ih2 =>
2437added intro heq hp
2438added injection heq with e1 e2
2439added subst e1 e2
2440added exact ih2 rfl (hhoare _ _ hc ⟨hp, hb⟩)
2441added | skip s0 => intro heq; simp at heq
2442added | asgn s0 a n x h => intro heq; simp at heq
2443added | seq c1 c2 s0 s0' s0'' h1 h2 ih1 ih2 => intro heq; simp at heq
2444added | ifTrue s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2445added | ifFalse s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2446added exact key _ st st' heval rfl hP
2447added
2448added-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00, before next release, 2021):
2449added-- This definition / discussion could be clearer.
2450added
2451added-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00, before next release, 2023):
2452added-- `Maja says: The wording of "we will never enter the
2453added-- loop" could definitely be improved. As is, it suggests a situation
2454added-- where the loop condition itself can never be satisfied. I suspect that
2455added-- a previous draft included a discussion that explicitly placed {{P}}
2456added-- before the while, perhaps along the lines of "a loop invariant P of
2457added-- [while b do c end] is also an invariant of [while b do c end]" (which
2458added-- is, FWIW, a (somewhat obtuse) way of stating a weaker variant of
2459added-- hoare_while, without the ~b in the postcondition). Combined with the
2460added-- fact that it is supposed to justify a somewhat surprising and
2461added-- unexpected fact — [X = 0] is not what I would intuitively consider an
2462added-- invariant of this loop — this sentence ends up being quite confusing.
2463added-- I only understood it when I came back to find this excerpt.`
2464added
2465added-- We call `P` a *loop invariant* of `while b do c end` if
2466added
2467added-- {{P ∧ b}} c {{P}}
2468added
2469added-- is a valid Hoare triple.
2470added
2471added-- This means that `P` will be true at the end of the loop body whenever the
2472added-- loop body executes. If `P` contradicts `b`, this holds trivially since the
2473added-- precondition is false.
2474added
2475added-- For instance, `X = 0` is a loop invariant of
2476added
2477added-- while X = 2 do X := 1 end
2478added
2479added-- since the program will never enter the loop.
2480added
2481added-- _Quiz:_
2482added
2483added-- Is the assertion
2484added
2485added-- Y = 0
2486added
2487added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2488added
2489added-- while X < 100 do X := X + 1 end
2490added
2491added-- (A) Yes
2492added
2493added-- (B) No
2494added
2495added-- _Quiz:_
2496added
2497added-- Is the assertion
2498added
2499added-- X = 0
2500added
2501added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2502added
2503added-- while X < 100 do X := X + 1 end
2504added
2505added-- (A) Yes
2506added
2507added-- (B) No
2508added
2509added-- _Quiz:_
2510added
2511added-- Is the assertion
2512added
2513added-- X < Y
2514added
2515added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2516added
2517added-- while true do X := X + 1; Y := Y + 1 end
2518added
2519added-- (A) Yes
2520added
2521added-- (B) No
2522added
2523added-- _Quiz:_
2524added
2525added-- Is the assertion
2526added
2527added-- X = Y + Z
2528added
2529added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2530added
2531added-- while Y > 10 do Y := Y - 1; Z := Z + 1 end
2532added
2533added-- (A) Yes
2534added
2535added-- (B) No
2536added
2537added-- Note to developers (before next release):
2538added-- This last quiz should be turned into a discussion in the text, at least
2539added-- in the full version -- indeed, maybe all these should be turned into a
2540added-- long discussion of what it means to be a loop invariant -- I think that
2541added-- would be pretty helpful.
2542added
2543added-- The program
2544added
2545added-- while Y > 10 do Y := Y - 1; Z := Z + 1 end
2546added
2547added-- admits an interesting loop invariant:
2548added
2549added-- X = Y + Z
2550added
2551added-- Note that this doesn't contradict the loop guard but neither is it a
2552added-- command invariant of
2553added
2554added-- Y := Y - 1; Z := Z + 1
2555added
2556added-- since, if X = 5, Y = 0 and Z = 5, running the command will set Y + Z to 6.
2557added-- The loop guard `Y > 10` guarantees that this will not be the case. We will
2558added-- see many such loop invariants in the following chapter.
2559added
2560added-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00, before next release, 2021):
2561added-- What is this example doing here?? Needs some text.
2562added
2563addedtheorem while_example :
2564added {{X ≤ 3}}
2565added while (X ≤ 2) {
2566added X := X + 1;
2567added }
2568added {{X = 3}} := by
2569added apply hoare_consequence_post
2570added · apply hoare_while
2571added apply hoare_consequence_pre
2572added · apply hoare_asgn
2573added · assertion_auto'
2574added · assertion_auto'
2575added
2576added-- Note to developers:
2577added-- `HIDE: CJC: Maybe also a good place to talk about the structure of
2578added-- our logic - that we've set up the hoare_* lemmas and they are all
2579added-- the reasoning about Hoare triples that they should have to use (in
2580added-- both formal or informal proofs)? Probably should talk about this
2581added-- somewhere or else we'll get back lots of proofs that unfold
2582added-- ValidHoareTriple and reason at a low level everywhere.
2583added--
2584added-- BCP 21: I think we do this now?`
2585added
2586added-- _Quiz:_
2587added
2588added-- Is the assertion
2589added
2590added-- X > 0
2591added
2592added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2593added
2594added-- while X = 0 do X := X - 1 end
2595added
2596added-- (A) Yes
2597added
2598added-- (B) No
2599added
2600added-- _Quiz:_
2601added
2602added-- Is the assertion
2603added
2604added-- X < 100
2605added
2606added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2607added
2608added-- while X < 100 do X := X + 1 end
2609added
2610added-- (A) Yes
2611added
2612added-- (B) No
2613added
2614added-- _Quiz:_
2615added
2616added-- Is the assertion
2617added
2618added-- X > 10
2619added
2620added-- a loop invariant of the following?
2621added
2622added-- while X > 10 do X := X + 1 end
2623added
2624added-- (A) Yes
2625added
2626added-- (B) No
2627added
2628added-- If the loop never terminates, any postcondition will work.
2629added
2630addedtheorem always_loop_hoare (Q : Assertion) :
2631added {{True}} while (true) { skip; } {{Q}} := by
2632added apply hoare_consequence_post
2633added · apply hoare_while
2634added apply hoare_post_true
2635added intro st
2636added exact True.intro
2637added · intro st ⟨_hinv, hguard⟩
2638added exact absurd rfl hguard
2639added
2640added-- Of course, this result is not surprising if we remember that the definition
2641added-- of `ValidHoareTriple` asserts that the postcondition must hold *only* when
2642added-- the command terminates. If the command doesn't terminate, we can prove
2643added-- anything we like about the post-condition.
2644added
2645added-- Hoare rules that specify what happens *if* commands terminate, without
2646added-- proving that they do, are said to describe a logic of *partial*
2647added-- correctness. It is also possible to give Hoare rules for *total*
2648added-- correctness, which additionally specifies that commands must terminate.
2649added-- Total correctness is out of the scope of this textbook.
2650added
2651added-- #### Exercise: `repeat`
2652added
2653added-- Note to developers:
2654added-- HIDE: I (BCP) think I see a much simpler way to do the 'for' stuff.
2655added-- Instead of `for x from a to b do c` define `for x downfrom a do c` that
2656added-- steps from a down to 0. This will be much simpler to specify, though
2657added-- still an interesting challenge. (CJC: This still seemed hard to me, but
2658added-- I'm deleting it for now to get things looking right)
2659added--
2660added-- HIDE: Coming up with the precise rule for REPEAT is tricky, and so is
2661added-- proving formally that the precise rule passes the litmus test (at this
2662added-- point we only ask them to convince themselves informally there).
2663added
2664added-- In this exercise, we'll add a new command to our language of commands:
2665added-- `repeat { c } until (b)`. You will write the evaluation rule for `repeat`
2666added-- and add a new Hoare rule to the language for programs involving it.
2667added
2668addednamespace RepeatExercise
2669added
2670addedinductive Com : Type where
2671added | skip : Com
2672added | asgn : Ident → Aexp → Com
2673added | seq : Com → Com → Com
2674added | cond : Bexp → Com → Com → Com
2675added | whileDo : Bexp → Com → Com
2676added | repeatUntil : Com → Bexp → Com
2677added
2678added-- `repeat` behaves like `while`, except that the loop guard is checked
2679added-- *after* each execution of the body, with the loop repeating as long as the
2680added-- guard stays *false*. Because of this, the body will always execute at least
2681added-- once.
2682added
2683added/-- Repeat-Imp commands: Imp commands plus `repeat` -/
2684addeddeclare_syntax_cat rpt_com
2685added/-- Repeat loop -/
2686addedsyntax "repeat" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") " until " "(" imp_bexp ")" : rpt_com
2687added
2688added/-- The command that does nothing (`skip;`) -/
2689addedsyntax ident ";" : rpt_com
2690added/-- Sequencing: one command after another -/
2691addedsyntax rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine rpt_com) : rpt_com
2692added/-- Assignment -/
2693addedsyntax ident " := " imp_aexp ";" : rpt_com
2694added/-- Conditional -/
2695addedsyntax "if " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine "}" ppHardSpace "else" ppHardSpace "{") ppLine rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : rpt_com
2696added/-- Loop -/
2697addedsyntax "while " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : rpt_com
2698added/-- Escape to Lean -/
2699addedsyntax:max "~" term:max : rpt_com
2700added
2701added/-- Include a Repeat-Imp command in Lean code -/
2702addedsyntax:min "impr" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine rpt_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : term
2703added
2704addedopen Lean in
2705addedmacro_rules
2706added | `(impr { $x:ident ; }) =>
2707added if x.getId == `skip then `(Com.skip)
2708added else Macro.throwErrorAt x s!"expected 'skip', got '{x.getId}'"
2709added | `(impr { $c1 $c2 }) =>
2710added `(Com.seq (impr {$c1}) (impr {$c2}))
2711added | `(impr { $x:ident := $a; }) =>
2712added `(Com.asgn $x (aexp {$a}))
2713added | `(impr { if ($b) {$c1} else {$c2} }) =>
2714added `(Com.cond (bexp {$b}) (impr {$c1}) (impr {$c2}))
2715added | `(impr { while ($b) {$c} }) =>
2716added `(Com.whileDo (bexp {$b}) (impr {$c}))
2717added | `(impr { repeat {$c} until ($b) }) =>
2718added `(Com.repeatUntil (impr {$c}) (bexp {$b}))
2719added | `(impr { ~$c }) =>
2720added pure c
2721added
2722added-- ### Exercise (4 stars): hoare_repeat (Advanced, manually graded) ⭐⭐⭐⭐
2723added
2724added-- Add new rules for `repeat` to `Com.EvalR` below. You can use the rules for
2725added-- `while` as a guide, but remember that the body of a `repeat` should always
2726added-- execute at least once, and that the loop ends when the guard becomes true.
2727added
2728addedinductive Com.EvalR : Com → State → State → Prop where
2729added | skip (st : State) :
2730added EvalR (impr {skip;}) st st
2731added | asgn (st : State) (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) (x : Ident) (h : a.eval st = n) :
2732added EvalR (impr {x := ~a;}) st (x →ₜ n ; st)
2733added | seq (c1 c2 : Com) (st st' st'' : State)
2734added (h1 : EvalR c1 st st') (h2 : EvalR c2 st' st'') :
2735added EvalR (impr {~c1 ~c2}) st st''
2736added | ifTrue (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = true)
2737added (hc : EvalR c1 st st') :
2738added EvalR (impr {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st st'
2739added | ifFalse (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false)
2740added (hc : EvalR c2 st st') :
2741added EvalR (impr {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st st'
2742added | whileFalse (b : Bexp) (st : State) (c : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false) :
2743added EvalR (impr {while (~b) {~c} }) st st
2744added | whileTrue (st st' st'' : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
2745added (hb : b.eval st = true) (hc : EvalR c st st')
2746added (hloop : EvalR (impr {while (~b) {~c} }) st' st'') :
2747added EvalR (impr {while (~b) {~c} }) st st''
2748added | repeatEnd (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com) (hc : EvalR c st st')
2749added (hb : b.eval st' = true) :
2750added EvalR (impr {repeat {~c} until (~b) }) st st'
2751added | repeatLoop (st st' st'' : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
2752added (hc : EvalR c st st') (hb : b.eval st' = false)
2753added (hloop : EvalR (impr {repeat {~c} until (~b) }) st' st'') :
2754added EvalR (impr {repeat {~c} until (~b) }) st st''
2755added
2756addedscoped notation:40 (priority := high) st0:41 " =[ " c " ]=> " st1:41 =>
2757added Com.EvalR c st0 st1
2758addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high) term:41 " =[ " rpt_com " ]=> " term:41 : term
2759addedscoped macro_rules
2760added | `($st0 =[ $c:rpt_com ]=> $st1) => `($st0 =[ impr { $c } ]=> $st1)

2762added-- A couple of definitions from above, copied here so they use the new
2763added-- `Com.EvalR`.
2764added
2765addeddef ValidHoareTriple (P : Assertion) (c : Com) (Q : Assertion) : Prop :=
2766added ∀ st st', (st =[ c ]=> st') → P st → Q st'
2767added
2768added/-- Hoare triple over Repeat-Imp commands -/
2769addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high)
2770added "{{" assn "}}" atomic(ppHardSpace rpt_com ppHardSpace "{{") assn "}}" : term
2771added
2772addedscoped macro_rules
2773added | `({{ $P }} $c:rpt_com {{ $Q }}) =>
2774added `(ValidHoareTriple ({{ $P }}) (impr { $c }) ({{ $Q }}))
2775added
2776added-- To make sure you've got the evaluation rules for `repeat` right, prove that
2777added-- `ex1_repeat` evaluates correctly.
2778added
2779addeddef ex1_repeat : Com :=
2780added impr {
2781added repeat {
2782added X := 1;
2783added Y := Y + 1;
2784added } until (X = 1)
2785added }
2786added
2787addedtheorem ex1_repeat_works :
2788added ∅ =[ ex1_repeat ]=> (Y →ₜ 1 ; X →ₜ 1 ; ∅) := by
2789added all_goals
2790added apply Com.EvalR.repeatEnd
2791added · apply Com.EvalR.seq
2792added · apply Com.EvalR.asgn; rfl
2793added · apply Com.EvalR.asgn; rfl
2794added · rfl
2795added
2796added-- Now state and prove a theorem, `hoare_repeat`, that expresses an
2797added-- appropriate proof rule for `repeat` commands. Use `hoare_while` as a model,
2798added-- and try to make your rule as precise as possible.
2799added
2800added/- Here is a very precise version of `hoare_repeat`. -/
2801added/- LATER: A student in 2013 pointed out that this rule is OK as far
2802addedas it goes, but it isn't going to lead to a nice rule for decorated
2803addedprograms, when we get to that, because it uses c twice, perhaps in
2804addeddifferent ways! -/
2805added
2806addedtheorem hoare_repeat (P Q : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
2807added (h1 : {{ P }} ~c {{ Q }}) (h2 : {{ Q ∧ ¬b }} ~c {{ Q }}) :
2808added {{ P }} repeat { ~c } until (~b) {{ Q ∧ b }} := by
2809added have key : ∀ (cmd : Com) (s s' : State), (s =[ cmd ]=> s') →
2810added cmd = (impr { repeat { ~c } until (~b) }) →
2811added ∀ (P' : Assertion), ({{ P' }} ~c {{ Q }}) → P' s →
2812added Q s' ∧ bassertion b s' := by
2813added intro cmd s s' hev
2814added induction hev with
2815added | repeatEnd s0 s0' b0 c0 hc hb =>
2816added intro heq P' hP'c hp
2817added injection heq with e1 e2
2818added subst e1 e2
2819added exact ⟨hP'c _ _ hc hp, hb⟩
2820added | repeatLoop s0 s0' s0'' b0 c0 hc hb hloop ih1 ih2 =>
2821added intro heq P' hP'c hp
2822added injection heq with e1 e2
2823added subst e1 e2
2824added apply ih2 rfl _ h2
2825added exact ⟨hP'c _ _ hc hp, bexp_eval_false _ _ hb⟩
2826added | skip s0 => intro heq; simp at heq
2827added | asgn s0 a n x h => intro heq; simp at heq
2828added | seq c1 c2 s0 s0' s0'' hh1 hh2 ih1 ih2 => intro heq; simp at heq
2829added | ifTrue s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2830added | ifFalse s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2831added | whileFalse b0 s0 c0 hb => intro heq; simp at heq
2832added | whileTrue s0 s0' s0'' b0 c0 hb hc hloop ih1 ih2 =>
2833added intro heq; simp at heq
2834added intro st st' heval hpre
2835added exact key _ st st' heval rfl P h1 hpre
2836added
2837added-- For full credit, make sure (informally) that your rule can be used to prove
2838added-- the following valid Hoare triple:
2839added
2840added-- {{ X > 0 }}
2841added-- repeat {
2842added-- Y := X;
2843added-- X := X - 1;
2844added-- } until (X = 0)
2845added-- {{ X = 0 ∧ Y > 0 }}
2846added
2847added-- Note to developers (Claude):
2848added-- The Rocq exercise region extends to End RepeatExercise. The directive
2849added-- here covers only the part up to the litmus-test display because Verso
2850added-- cannot compile the whole module as one block.
2851added
2852added/- Although it was not required by the exercise, we can show formally
2853addedthat `hoare_repeat` can handle this litmus test: -/
2854added
2855addeddef ex2_repeat : Com :=
2856added impr {
2857added repeat {
2858added Y := X;
2859added X := X - 1;
2860added } until (X = 0)
2861added }
2862added
2863added/- Before we can show anything about this program we need to repeat
2864addedthe proofs of some more Hoare rules from above (remember we're in
2865addeda separate namespace, with a different definition of commands). -/
2866added
2867addedtheorem hoare_asgn (Q : Assertion) (x : Ident) (a : Aexp) :
2868added {{Q [x ↦ ~a]}} x := ~a; {{Q}} := by
2869added unfold ValidHoareTriple
2870added intro st st' hE hQ
2871added inversion hE with
2872added | asgn n h =>
2873added subst h
2874added exact hQ
2875added
2876addedtheorem hoare_consequence (P P' Q Q' : Assertion) (c : Com)
2877added (hht : {{P'}} ~c {{Q'}}) (hPP' : P ->> P') (hQ'Q : Q' ->> Q) :
2878added {{P}} ~c {{Q}} := by
2879added intro st st' hc hP
2880added apply hQ'Q
2881added apply hht st st'
2882added · assumption
2883added · apply hPP'
2884added assumption
2885added
2886addedtheorem hoare_consequence_pre (P P' Q : Assertion) (c : Com)
2887added (hhoare : {{P'}} ~c {{Q}}) (himp : P ->> P') :
2888added {{P}} ~c {{Q}} := by
2889added intro st st' hc hP
2890added apply hhoare st st'
2891added · assumption
2892added · apply himp
2893added assumption
2894added
2895addedtheorem hoare_seq (P Q R : Assertion) (c1 c2 : Com)
2896added (h1 : {{Q}} ~c2 {{R}}) (h2 : {{P}} ~c1 {{Q}}) :
2897added {{P}} ~c1 ~c2 {{R}} := by
2898added intro st st' h12 pre
2899added inversion h12 with
2900added | seq st'' hc1 hc2 =>
2901added exact h1 _ _ hc2 (h2 _ _ hc1 pre)
2902added
2903added/- Now we are ready to show `ex2_repeat` correct using `hoare_repeat`. -/
2904added/- NOTATION: IY -- I've noticed this oddity in previous lemmas, but
2905addedit's especially noticable here that an explicit state is given to
2906addedthe conditional statements. -/
2907addedtheorem ex2_repeat_hoare_repeat :
2908added {{ X > 0 }}
2909added ~ex2_repeat
2910added {{ X = 0 ∧ Y > 0 }} := by
2911added unfold ex2_repeat
2912added apply hoare_consequence
2913added · apply hoare_repeat (Q := {{ Y > 0 }})
2914added · apply hoare_seq <;> apply hoare_asgn
2915added · apply hoare_seq
2916added · apply hoare_asgn
2917added · apply hoare_consequence_pre
2918added · apply hoare_asgn
2919added · assertion_auto'
2920added · -- body of repeat if exiting right away
2921added assertion_auto'
2922added · -- final postcondition
2923added assertion_auto'
2924added
2925added/- A sound but less precise variant of the `hoare_repeat` rule looks
2926addedlike this: -/
2927added
2928added/- NOTATION: Here, too, the printing isn't as we write the notation.
2929added(As soon as we start the proof context). Is this intended? -/
2930addedtheorem hoare_repeat' (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
2931added (h : {{P}} ~c {{P}}) :
2932added {{P}} repeat { ~c } until (~b) {{ P ∧ b }} := by
2933added unfold ValidHoareTriple
2934added intro st st' he hP
2935added have key : ∀ (cmd : Com) (s s' : State), (s =[ cmd ]=> s') →
2936added cmd = (impr { repeat { ~c } until (~b) }) → P s →
2937added P s' ∧ bassertion b s' := by
2938added intro cmd s s' hev
2939added induction hev with
2940added | repeatEnd s0 s0' b0 c0 hc hb =>
2941added intro heq hp
2942added injection heq with e1 e2
2943added subst e1 e2
2944added exact ⟨h _ _ hc hp, hb⟩
2945added | repeatLoop s0 s0' s0'' b0 c0 hc hb hloop ih1 ih2 =>
2946added intro heq hp
2947added injection heq with e1 e2
2948added subst e1 e2
2949added exact ih2 rfl (h _ _ hc hp)
2950added | skip s0 => intro heq; simp at heq
2951added | asgn s0 a n x ha => intro heq; simp at heq
2952added | seq c1 c2 s0 s0' s0'' hh1 hh2 ih1 ih2 => intro heq; simp at heq
2953added | ifTrue s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2954added | ifFalse s0 s0' b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
2955added | whileFalse b0 s0 c0 hb => intro heq; simp at heq
2956added | whileTrue s0 s0' s0'' b0 c0 hb hc hloop ih1 ih2 =>
2957added intro heq; simp at heq
2958added exact key _ st st' he rfl hP
2959added
2960added/- First, let's show that `hoare_repeat'` is implied by `hoare_repeat`. -/
2961added
2962addedtheorem hoare_repeat_implies_hoare_repeat'
2963added (hoare_repeat : ∀ (P Q : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com),
2964added ({{ P }} ~c {{ Q }}) →
2965added ({{ Q ∧ ¬b }} ~c {{ Q }}) →
2966added {{ P }} repeat { ~c } until (~b) {{ Q ∧ b }}) :
2967added ∀ (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com),
2968added ({{P}} ~c {{P}}) →
2969added {{P}} repeat { ~c } until (~b) {{ P ∧ b }} := by
2970added intro P b c h
2971added apply hoare_repeat <;> try assumption
2972added apply hoare_consequence_pre
2973added · exact h
2974added · intro st ⟨hp, _⟩
2975added exact hp
2976added
2977added/- However, we can't prove `ex2_repeat` correct using `hoare_repeat'`,

2981addedexample :

2986added · apply hoare_repeat' (P := {{ Y > 0 }})
2987added apply hoare_seq
2988added · apply hoare_asgn
2989added · apply hoare_consequence_pre

2991added · -- body of repeat if looping
2992added unfold AssertImplies Assertion.sub
2993added intro st hy
2994added -- loop invariant too weak on its own,
2995added -- we need the value of the previous guard
2996added sorry
2997added · -- initial precondition
2998added intro st ⟨_, hy⟩
2999added exact hy
3000added -- this only works with an additional Y > 0 precondition
3001added · -- final postcondition

3003added
3004added/- Here is a second failed attempt trying stronger loop invariant, but
3005addedit is too strong. -/
3006added
3007addedexample :

3011added apply hoare_consequence
3012added · apply hoare_repeat' (P := {{ X > 0 ∧ Y > 0 }})
3013added apply hoare_seq

3015added · apply hoare_consequence_pre

3019added intro st ⟨hx, hy⟩

3022added · -- initial precondition

3029added
3030added-- ## Summary
3031added
3032added-- So far, we've introduced Hoare Logic as a tool for reasoning about Imp
3033added-- programs.
3034added
3035added-- The rules of Hoare Logic are:
3036added
3037added-- --------------------------- (hoare_asgn)
3038added-- {{Q [X ↦ a]}} X:=a {{Q}}
3039added
3040added-- -------------------- (hoare_skip)
3041added-- {{ P }} skip {{ P }}
3042added
3043added-- {{ P }} c1 {{ Q }}
3044added-- {{ Q }} c2 {{ R }}
3045added-- ---------------------- (hoare_seq)
3046added-- {{ P }} c1;c2 {{ R }}
3047added
3048added-- {{P ∧ b}} c1 {{Q}}
3049added-- {{P ∧ ¬ b}} c2 {{Q}}
3050added-- ------------------------------------ (hoare_if)
3051added-- {{P}} if b then c1 else c2 end {{Q}}
3052added
3053added-- {{P ∧ b}} c {{P}}
3054added-- ----------------------------------- (hoare_while)
3055added-- {{P}} while b do c end {{P ∧ ¬ b}}
3056added
3057added-- {{P'}} c {{Q'}}
3058added-- P ->> P'
3059added-- Q' ->> Q
3060added-- ----------------------------- (hoare_consequence)
3061added-- {{P}} c {{Q}}
3062added
3063added-- Our main task in this chapter has been to *define* the rules of Hoare
3064added-- logic, and prove that the definitions are sound. Having done so, we can go
3065added-- on and work *within* Hoare logic to prove that particular programs satisfy
3066added-- particular Hoare triples. In the next chapter, we'll see how Hoare logic is
3067added-- can be used to prove that more interesting programs satisfy interesting
3068added-- specifications of their behavior.
3069added
3070added-- Crucially, we will do so without ever again `unfold`ing the definition of
3071added-- Hoare triples -- i.e., we will take the rules of Hoare logic as a closed
3072added-- world for reasoning about programs.
3073added
3074added-- ## Additional Exercises
3075added
3076added-- ### Havoc
3077added
3078added-- In this exercise, we will derive proof rules for a `havoc` command, which
3079added-- is similar to the nondeterministic `any` expression from the the Imp
3080added-- chapter.
3081added
3082added-- First, we enclose this work in a separate namespace, and recall the syntax
3083added-- and big-step semantics of Himp commands.
3084added
3085addednamespace Himp
3086added
3087addedinductive Com : Type where
3088added | skip : Com
3089added | asgn : Ident → Aexp → Com
3090added | seq : Com → Com → Com
3091added | cond : Bexp → Com → Com → Com
3092added | whileDo : Bexp → Com → Com
3093added | havoc : Ident → Com
3094added
3095added/-- Himp commands: Imp commands plus `havoc` -/
3096addeddeclare_syntax_cat himp_com
3097added/-- Havoc: set a variable to a nondeterministically chosen number
3098added(`havoc x;`). As with `skip`, the word `havoc` is not reserved: the
3099addedproduction accepts any identifier and the macro below rejects
3100addedeverything except `havoc`. -/
3101addedsyntax ident ident ";" : himp_com
3102added
3103added/-- The command that does nothing (`skip;`) -/
3104addedsyntax ident ";" : himp_com
3105added/-- Sequencing: one command after another -/
3106addedsyntax himp_com ppDedent(ppLine himp_com) : himp_com
3107added/-- Assignment -/
3108addedsyntax ident " := " imp_aexp ";" : himp_com
3109added/-- Conditional -/
3110addedsyntax "if " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine himp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}" ppHardSpace "else" ppHardSpace "{") ppLine himp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : himp_com
3111added/-- Loop -/
3112addedsyntax "while " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine himp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : himp_com
3113added/-- Escape to Lean -/
3114addedsyntax:max "~" term:max : himp_com
3115added
3116added/-- Include a Himp command in Lean code -/
3117addedsyntax:min "imph" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine himp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : term
3118added
3119addedopen Lean in
3120addedmacro_rules
3121added | `(imph { $x:ident ; }) =>
3122added if x.getId == `skip then `(Com.skip)
3123added else Macro.throwErrorAt x s!"expected 'skip', got '{x.getId}'"
3124added | `(imph { $c1 $c2 }) =>
3125added `(Com.seq (imph {$c1}) (imph {$c2}))
3126added | `(imph { $x:ident := $a; }) =>
3127added `(Com.asgn $x (aexp {$a}))
3128added | `(imph { if ($b) {$c1} else {$c2} }) =>
3129added `(Com.cond (bexp {$b}) (imph {$c1}) (imph {$c2}))
3130added | `(imph { while ($b) {$c} }) =>
3131added `(Com.whileDo (bexp {$b}) (imph {$c}))
3132added | `(imph { $h:ident $x:ident ; }) =>
3133added if h.getId == `havoc then `(Com.havoc $x)
3134added else Macro.throwErrorAt h s!"expected 'havoc', got '{h.getId}'"
3135added | `(imph { ~$c }) =>
3136added pure c
3137added
3138addedinductive Com.EvalR : Com → State → State → Prop where
3139added | skip (st : State) :
3140added EvalR (imph {skip;}) st st
3141added | asgn (st : State) (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) (x : Ident) (h : a.eval st = n) :
3142added EvalR (imph {x := ~a;}) st (x →ₜ n ; st)
3143added | seq (c1 c2 : Com) (st st' st'' : State)
3144added (h1 : EvalR c1 st st') (h2 : EvalR c2 st' st'') :
3145added EvalR (imph {~c1 ~c2}) st st''
3146added | ifTrue (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = true)
3147added (hc : EvalR c1 st st') :
3148added EvalR (imph {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st st'
3149added | ifFalse (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false)
3150added (hc : EvalR c2 st st') :
3151added EvalR (imph {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st st'
3152added | whileFalse (b : Bexp) (st : State) (c : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false) :
3153added EvalR (imph {while (~b) {~c} }) st st
3154added | whileTrue (st st' st'' : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
3155added (hb : b.eval st = true) (hc : EvalR c st st')
3156added (hloop : EvalR (imph {while (~b) {~c} }) st' st'') :
3157added EvalR (imph {while (~b) {~c} }) st st''
3158added | havoc (st : State) (x : Ident) (n : Nat) :
3159added EvalR (imph {havoc x;}) st (x →ₜ n ; st)
3160added
3161addedscoped notation:40 (priority := high) st0:41 " =[ " c " ]=> " st1:41 =>
3162added Com.EvalR c st0 st1
3163addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high) term:41 " =[ " himp_com " ]=> " term:41 : term
3164addedscoped macro_rules
3165added | `($st0 =[ $c:himp_com ]=> $st1) => `($st0 =[ imph { $c } ]=> $st1)
3166added
3167added-- The definition of Hoare triples is exactly as before.
3168added
3169addeddef ValidHoareTriple (P : Assertion) (c : Com) (Q : Assertion) : Prop :=
3170added ∀ st st', (st =[ c ]=> st') → P st → Q st'
3171added
3172added/-- Hoare triple over Himp commands -/
3173addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high)
3174added "{{" assn "}}" atomic(ppHardSpace himp_com ppHardSpace "{{") assn "}}" : term
3175added
3176addedscoped macro_rules
3177added | `({{ $P }} $c:himp_com {{ $Q }}) =>
3178added `(ValidHoareTriple ({{ $P }}) (imph { $c }) ({{ $Q }}))
3179added
3180added-- And the precondition consequence rule is exactly as before.
3181added
3182addedtheorem hoare_consequence_pre (P P' Q : Assertion) (c : Com)
3183added (hhoare : {{P'}} ~c {{Q}}) (himp : P ->> P') :
3184added {{P}} ~c {{Q}} := by
3185added intro st st' heval hpre
3186added exact hhoare st st' heval (himp st hpre)
3187added
3188added-- ### Exercise (3 stars): hoare_havoc (Advanced) ⭐⭐⭐
3189added
3190added-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00, before next release, 2021):
3191added-- This exercise turns out to be quite hard -- a lot of people get stuck.
3192added-- We should make it advanced the next time through. BCP 23: Made it
3193added-- advanced. Can we also explain it better?
3194added
3195added-- Complete the Hoare rule for `havoc` commands below by defining `havoc_pre`,
3196added-- and prove that the resulting rule is correct.
3197added
3198addeddef havoc_pre (x : Ident) (Q : Assertion) (st : State) : Prop :=
3199added (∀ (n : Nat), Assertion.sub x (.num n) Q st)
3200added
3201addedtheorem hoare_havoc (Q : Assertion) (x : Ident) :
3202added {{ ~(havoc_pre x Q) }} havoc x; {{ Q }} := by
3203added all_goals
3204added unfold ValidHoareTriple havoc_pre
3205added intro st st' heval hpre
3206added inversion heval with
3207added | havoc n => apply hpre
3208added
3209added-- ### Exercise (3 stars): havoc_post (Advanced) ⭐⭐⭐
3210added
3211added-- Complete the following proof without changing any of the provided commands.
3212added-- If you find that it can't be completed, your definition of `havoc_pre` is
3213added-- probably too strong. Find a way to relax it so that `havoc_post` can be
3214added-- proved.
3215added
3216added-- Hint: the `assertion_auto` tactics we've built won't help you here. You
3217added-- need to proceed manually.
3218added
3219added-- Note to developers (before next release):
3220added-- This exercise is kind of weird. Should probably be optional.
3221added
3222addedtheorem havoc_post (P : Assertion) (x : Ident) :
3223added {{ P }} havoc x;
3224added {{ ~(fun st => ∃ (n : Nat), ({{ P [x ↦ ~(Aexp.num n)] }}) st) }} := by
3225added apply hoare_consequence_pre
3226added · apply hoare_havoc
3227added ·
3228added all_goals
3229added unfold havoc_pre AssertImplies Assertion.sub
3230added intro st hP n
3231added exists st[x]
3232added rw [TotalMap.update_shadow]

3239added-- ### Assert and Assume
3240added
3241added-- Note to developers (Claude):
3242added-- The Rocq exercise region extends to End HoareAssertAssume. The
3243added-- directive here covers only the initial student tasks because Verso
3244added-- cannot compile the whole module as one block.
3245added
3246added-- In this exercise, we will extend IMP with two commands, `assert` and
3247added-- `assume`. Both commands are ways to indicate that a certain assertion
3248added-- should hold any time this part of the program is reached. However they
3249added-- differ as follows:
3250added
3251added-- - If an `assert` statement fails, it causes the program to go into an error
3252added-- state and exit.
3253added
3254added-- - If an `assume` statement fails, the program fails to evaluate at all. In
3255added-- other words, the program gets stuck and has no final state.
3256added
3257added-- The new set of commands is:
3258added
3259addednamespace HoareAssertAssume
3260added
3261addedinductive Com : Type where
3262added | skip : Com
3263added | asgn : Ident → Aexp → Com
3264added | seq : Com → Com → Com
3265added | cond : Bexp → Com → Com → Com
3266added | whileDo : Bexp → Com → Com
3267added | assert : Bexp → Com
3268added | assume : Bexp → Com
3269added
3270added-- Note to developers:
3271added-- NOTATION: LATER: Reconsider these precedences
3272added
3273added/-- Imp commands plus `assert` and `assume` -/
3274addeddeclare_syntax_cat haa_com
3275added/-- Assert / assume (`assert (b);`, `assume (b);`). As with `skip`, the
3276addedwords `assert` and `assume` are not reserved: the production accepts any
3277addedidentifier and the macro below rejects everything else. -/
3278addedsyntax ident " (" imp_bexp ")" ";" : haa_com
3279added
3280added/-- The command that does nothing (`skip;`) -/
3281addedsyntax ident ";" : haa_com
3282added/-- Sequencing: one command after another -/
3283addedsyntax haa_com ppDedent(ppLine haa_com) : haa_com
3284added/-- Assignment -/
3285addedsyntax ident " := " imp_aexp ";" : haa_com
3286added/-- Conditional -/
3287addedsyntax "if " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine haa_com ppDedent(ppLine "}" ppHardSpace "else" ppHardSpace "{") ppLine haa_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : haa_com
3288added/-- Loop -/
3289addedsyntax "while " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine haa_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : haa_com
3290added/-- Escape to Lean -/
3291addedsyntax:max "~" term:max : haa_com
3292added
3293added/-- Include an assert/assume-Imp command in Lean code -/
3294addedsyntax:min "impa" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine haa_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : term
3295added
3296addedopen Lean in
3297addedmacro_rules
3298added | `(impa { $x:ident ; }) =>
3299added if x.getId == `skip then `(Com.skip)
3300added else Macro.throwErrorAt x s!"expected 'skip', got '{x.getId}'"
3301added | `(impa { $h:ident ($b) ; }) =>
3302added if h.getId == `assert then `(Com.assert (bexp {$b}))
3303added else if h.getId == `assume then `(Com.assume (bexp {$b}))
3304added else Macro.throwErrorAt h s!"expected 'assert' or 'assume', got '{h.getId}'"
3305added | `(impa { $c1 $c2 }) =>
3306added `(Com.seq (impa {$c1}) (impa {$c2}))
3307added | `(impa { $x:ident := $a; }) =>
3308added `(Com.asgn $x (aexp {$a}))
3309added | `(impa { if ($b) {$c1} else {$c2} }) =>
3310added `(Com.cond (bexp {$b}) (impa {$c1}) (impa {$c2}))
3311added | `(impa { while ($b) {$c} }) =>
3312added `(Com.whileDo (bexp {$b}) (impa {$c}))
3313added | `(impa { ~$c }) =>
3314added pure c
3315added
3316added-- To define the behavior of `assert` and `assume`, we need to add notation
3317added-- for an error, which indicates that an assertion has failed. We modify the
3318added-- `Com.EvalR` relation, therefore, so that it relates a start state to either
3319added-- an end state or to `error`. The `Result` type indicates the end value of a
3320added-- program, either a state or an error:
3321added
3322addedinductive Result : Type where
3323added | normal : State → Result
3324added | error : Result
3325added
3326added-- Now we are ready to give you the evaluation relation for the new language.
3327added
3328addedinductive Com.EvalR : Com → State → Result → Prop where
3329added /- Old rules, several modified -/
3330added | skip (st : State) :
3331added EvalR (impa {skip;}) st (.normal st)
3332added | asgn (st : State) (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) (x : Ident) (h : a.eval st = n) :
3333added EvalR (impa {x := ~a;}) st (.normal (x →ₜ n ; st))
3334added | seqNormal (c1 c2 : Com) (st st' : State) (r : Result)
3335added (h1 : EvalR c1 st (.normal st')) (h2 : EvalR c2 st' r) :
3336added EvalR (impa {~c1 ~c2}) st r
3337added | seqError (c1 c2 : Com) (st : State) (h : EvalR c1 st .error) :
3338added EvalR (impa {~c1 ~c2}) st .error
3339added | ifTrue (st : State) (r : Result) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com)
3340added (hb : b.eval st = true) (hc : EvalR c1 st r) :
3341added EvalR (impa {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st r
3342added | ifFalse (st : State) (r : Result) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com)
3343added (hb : b.eval st = false) (hc : EvalR c2 st r) :
3344added EvalR (impa {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2} }) st r
3345added | whileFalse (b : Bexp) (st : State) (c : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false) :
3346added EvalR (impa {while (~b) {~c} }) st (.normal st)
3347added | whileTrueNormal (st st' : State) (r : Result) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
3348added (hb : b.eval st = true) (hc : EvalR c st (.normal st'))
3349added (hloop : EvalR (impa {while (~b) {~c} }) st' r) :
3350added EvalR (impa {while (~b) {~c} }) st r
3351added | whileTrueError (st : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
3352added (hb : b.eval st = true) (hc : EvalR c st .error) :
3353added EvalR (impa {while (~b) {~c} }) st .error
3354added /- Rules for Assert and Assume -/
3355added | assertTrue (st : State) (b : Bexp) (hb : b.eval st = true) :
3356added EvalR (impa {assert (~b);}) st (.normal st)
3357added | assertFalse (st : State) (b : Bexp) (hb : b.eval st = false) :
3358added EvalR (impa {assert (~b);}) st .error
3359added | assume (st : State) (b : Bexp) (hb : b.eval st = true) :
3360added EvalR (impa {assume (~b);}) st (.normal st)
3361added
3362addedscoped notation:40 (priority := high) st0:41 " =[ " c " ]=> " r:41 =>
3363added Com.EvalR c st0 r
3364addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high) term:41 " =[ " haa_com " ]=> " term:41 : term
3365addedscoped macro_rules
3366added | `($st0 =[ $c:haa_com ]=> $r) => `($st0 =[ impa { $c } ]=> $r)
3367added
3368added-- We redefine hoare triples: Now, `{{P}} c {{Q}}` means that, whenever `c` is
3369added-- started in a state satisfying `P`, and terminates with result `r`, then `r`
3370added-- is not an error and the state of `r` satisfies `Q`.
3371added
3372addeddef ValidHoareTriple
3373added (P : Assertion) (c : Com) (Q : Assertion) : Prop :=
3374added ∀ st r,
3375added (st =[ c ]=> r) → P st →
3376added (∃ st', r = Result.normal st' ∧ Q st')
3377added
3378added/-- Hoare triple over assert/assume-Imp commands -/
3379addedscoped syntax:40 (priority := high)
3380added "{{" assn "}}" atomic(ppHardSpace haa_com ppHardSpace "{{") assn "}}" : term
3381added
3382addedscoped macro_rules
3383added | `({{ $P }} $c:haa_com {{ $Q }}) =>
3384added `(ValidHoareTriple ({{ $P }}) (impa { $c }) ({{ $Q }}))
3385added
3386added-- ### Exercise (4 stars): assert_vs_assume ⭐⭐⭐⭐
3387added
3388added-- To test your understanding of this modification, give an example
3389added-- precondition and postcondition that are satisfied by the `assume` statement
3390added-- but not by the `assert` statement.
3391added
3392addedtheorem assert_assume_differ : ∃ (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (Q : Assertion),
3393added ({{P}} assume (~b); {{Q}})
3394added ∧ ¬ ({{P}} assert (~b); {{Q}}) := by
3395added all_goals
3396added exists {{True}}, bexp { false }, {{False}}
3397added constructor
3398added · unfold ValidHoareTriple
3399added intro st r hE _
3400added inversion hE with
3401added | assume hb => simp at hb
3402added · intro hC
3403added unfold ValidHoareTriple at hC
3404added have h : ∅ =[ assert (false); ]=> Result.error := by
3405added apply Com.EvalR.assertFalse
3406added rfl
3407added obtain ⟨st', heq, _⟩ := hC ∅ Result.error h True.intro
3408added simp at heq
3409added
3410added-- Then prove that any triple for an `assert` also works when `assert` is
3411added-- replaced by `assume`.
3412added
3413addedtheorem assert_implies_assume (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (Q : Assertion)
3414added (hhoare : {{P}} assert (~b); {{Q}}) :
3415added {{P}} assume (~b); {{Q}} := by
3416added all_goals
3417added unfold ValidHoareTriple
3418added intro st r hEval hP
3419added inversion hEval with
3420added | assume hb =>
3421added exists st
3422added have h : st =[ assert (~b); ]=> Result.normal st := by
3423added apply Com.EvalR.assertTrue
3424added assumption
3425added obtain ⟨st', h1, h2⟩ := hhoare st (Result.normal st) h hP
3426added injection h1 with e
3427added subst e
3428added exact ⟨rfl, h2⟩
3429added
3430added-- Next, here are proofs for the old hoare rules adapted to the new semantics.
3431added-- You don't need to do anything with these.
3432added
3433addedtheorem hoare_asgn (Q : Assertion) (x : Ident) (a : Aexp) :
3434added {{Q [x ↦ ~a]}} x := ~a; {{Q}} := by
3435added unfold ValidHoareTriple
3436added intro st r hE hQ
3437added inversion hE with
3438added | asgn n h =>
3439added exists (x →ₜ n ; st)
3440added subst h
3441added exact ⟨rfl, hQ⟩
3442added
3443addedtheorem hoare_consequence_pre (P P' Q : Assertion) (c : Com)
3444added (hhoare : {{P'}} ~c {{Q}}) (himp : P ->> P') :
3445added {{P}} ~c {{Q}} := by
3446added intro st r hc hP
3447added apply hhoare st r
3448added · assumption
3449added · apply himp
3450added assumption
3451added
3452addedtheorem hoare_consequence_post (P Q Q' : Assertion) (c : Com)
3453added (hhoare : {{P}} ~c {{Q'}}) (himp : Q' ->> Q) :
3454added {{P}} ~c {{Q}} := by
3455added intro st r hc hP
3456added unfold ValidHoareTriple at hhoare
3457added have h : ∃ st', r = Result.normal st' ∧ Q' st' := by
3458added apply hhoare st <;> assumption
3459added obtain ⟨st', hr, hQ'⟩ := h
3460added exists st'
3461added constructor
3462added · assumption
3463added · apply himp
3464added assumption
3465added
3466addedtheorem hoare_seq (P Q R : Assertion) (c1 c2 : Com)
3467added (h1 : {{Q}} ~c2 {{R}}) (h2 : {{P}} ~c1 {{Q}}) :
3468added {{P}} ~c1 ~c2 {{R}} := by
3469added intro st r h12 pre
3470added inversion h12 with
3471added | seqNormal st' hc1 hc2 =>
3472added apply h1
3473added · apply hc2
3474added · apply h2 at hc1
3475added apply hc1 at pre
3476added obtain ⟨st'', heq, hQ⟩ := pre
3477added injection heq with e
3478added subst e
3479added assumption
3480added | seqError hc1 =>
3481added -- Find contradictory assumption
3482added apply h2 at hc1
3483added apply hc1 at pre
3484added obtain ⟨st', hC, _⟩ := pre
3485added simp at hC
3486added
3487added-- Here are the other proof rules (sanity check)
3488added
3489addedtheorem hoare_skip (P : Assertion) :
3490added {{P}} skip; {{P}} := by
3491added intro st r h hP
3492added inversion h
3493added exact ⟨st, rfl, hP⟩
3494added
3495addedtheorem hoare_if (P Q : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com)
3496added (hTrue : {{ P ∧ b}} ~c1 {{Q}}) (hFalse : {{ P ∧ ¬b}} ~c2 {{Q}}) :
3497added {{P}} if (~b) { ~c1 } else { ~c2 } {{Q}} := by
3498added intro st r hE hP
3499added inversion hE with
3500added | ifTrue hb hc =>
3501added -- b is true
3502added apply hTrue st r
3503added · assumption
3504added · exact ⟨hP, hb⟩
3505added | ifFalse hb hc =>
3506added -- b is false
3507added apply hFalse st r
3508added · assumption
3509added · exact ⟨hP, bexp_eval_false b st hb⟩
3510added
3511addedtheorem hoare_while (P : Assertion) (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
3512added (hhoare : {{P ∧ b}} ~c {{P}}) :
3513added {{P}} while (~b) { ~c } {{ P ∧ ¬b}} := by
3514added intro st r he hP
3515added have key : ∀ (cmd : Com) (s : State) (r' : Result), (s =[ cmd ]=> r') →
3516added cmd = (impa { while (~b) { ~c } }) → P s →
3517added ∃ s', r' = Result.normal s' ∧ P s' ∧ ¬ bassertion b s' := by
3518added intro cmd s r' hev
3519added induction hev with
3520added | whileFalse b0 s0 c0 hb =>
3521added intro heq hp
3522added injection heq with e1 _
3523added subst e1
3524added exact ⟨s0, rfl, hp, bexp_eval_false _ _ hb⟩
3525added | whileTrueNormal s0 s0' r0 b0 c0 hb hc hloop ih1 ih2 =>
3526added intro heq hp
3527added injection heq with e1 e2
3528added subst e1 e2
3529added apply ih2 rfl
3530added obtain ⟨s1, heq1, hp1⟩ := hhoare _ _ hc ⟨hp, hb⟩
3531added injection heq1 with e
3532added subst e
3533added exact hp1
3534added | whileTrueError s0 b0 c0 hb hc =>
3535added intro heq hp
3536added injection heq with e1 e2
3537added subst e1 e2
3538added obtain ⟨s1, heq1, _⟩ := hhoare _ _ hc ⟨hp, hb⟩
3539added simp at heq1
3540added | skip s0 => intro heq; simp at heq
3541added | asgn s0 a n x ha => intro heq; simp at heq
3542added | seqNormal c1 c2 s0 s0' r0 hh1 hh2 ih1 ih2 => intro heq; simp at heq
3543added | seqError c1 c2 s0 hh ih => intro heq; simp at heq
3544added | ifTrue s0 r0 b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
3545added | ifFalse s0 r0 b0 c1 c2 hb hc ih => intro heq; simp at heq
3546added | assertTrue s0 b0 hb => intro heq; simp at heq
3547added | assertFalse s0 b0 hb => intro heq; simp at heq
3548added | assume s0 b0 hb => intro heq; simp at heq
3549added exact key _ st r he rfl hP
3550added
3551added-- Finally, state Hoare rules for `assert` and `assume` and use them to prove
3552added-- a simple program correct. Name your rules `hoare_assert` and
3553added-- `hoare_assume`.
3554added
3555added/- HIDE: Equivalently, we could make the postcondition Q ∧ b or the
3556addedprecondition Q → b ... -/
3557addedtheorem hoare_assert (Q : Assertion) (b : Bexp) :
3558added {{Q ∧ b}} assert (~b); {{Q}} := by
3559added intro st r hEval hpre
3560added obtain ⟨hst, hb⟩ := hpre
3561added exists st
3562added inversion hEval with
3563added | assertTrue hb' => exact ⟨rfl, hst⟩
3564added | assertFalse hb' => simp [bassertion, hb'] at hb
3565added
3566added/- Stating this in a backwards-direction friendly way. -/
3567added/- HIDE: Equivalently, we could make the postcondition Q ∧ b... -/
3568addedtheorem hoare_assume (Q : Assertion) (b : Bexp) :
3569added {{ b → Q }} assume (~b); {{Q}} := by
3570added intro st r hEval hst
3571added exists st
3572added inversion hEval with
3573added | assume hb => exact ⟨rfl, hst hb⟩
3574added
3575added-- Use your rules to prove the following triple.
3576added
3577addedtheorem assert_assume_example :
3578added {{True}}
3579added assume (X = 1);
3580added X := X + 1;
3581added assert (X = 2);
3582added {{True}} := by
3583added all_goals
3584added apply hoare_consequence_pre
3585added · apply hoare_seq
3586added · apply hoare_seq
3587added · apply hoare_assert
3588added · apply hoare_asgn
3589added · apply hoare_assume
3590added · assertion_auto'
3591added
3592addedend HoareAssertAssume
3593added

30added/--
31added `inversion t` generalizes nonvariable indices of the type of `t` before invoking `cases t`,
32added then solves away contradictory generated goals.
33added `t` itself will also be generalized with a heterogeneous equality `heq`
34added if trying to generalize the indices produces an ill-typed result.
35added * If `inversion +clear t` is set, then `heq` will be `clear`ed from the context if present,
36added along with `t` if there are no dependencies on it.
37added * The form `inversion t with | tag₁ x ... => tac ... | ... | tagₙ z ... => tac ...` is supported,
38added similar to that of `cases` and `inversion`.
39added-/

45addednamespace Lean.Meta
46added
47added/--
48added This function is similar to `forallMetaTelescopeReducing`: Given `e` of the
49added form `forall ..xs, A`, this combinator will create a new metavariable for
50added each `x` in `xs` until it reaches an `x` whose type is defeq to `t`,
51added and instantiate `A` with these, while also reducing `A` if needed.
52added It uses `forallMetaTelescopeReducing`.
53added
54added This function returns a triple `(mvs, bis, out)` where
55added - `mvs` is an array containing the new metavariables.
56added - `bis` is an array containing the binder infos for the `mvs`.
57added - `out` is `e` but instantiated with the `mvs`.
58added
59added Lifted from [https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Lean/Meta/Basic.lean#L41].
60added-/
61addeddef forallMetaTelescopeReducingUntilDefEq
62added (e t : Expr) (kind : MetavarKind := MetavarKind.natural) :
63added MetaM (Array Expr × Array BinderInfo × Expr) := do
64added let (ms, bs, tp) ← forallMetaTelescopeReducing e (some 1) kind
65added unless ms.size == 1 do
66added if ms.size == 0 then throwError m!"Failed: {← ppExpr e} is not the type of a function."
67added else throwError m!"Failed"
68added let mut mvs := ms
69added let mut bis := bs
70added let mut out : Expr := tp
71added while !(← isDefEq (← inferType mvs.toList.getLast!) t) do
72added let (ms, bs, tp) ← forallMetaTelescopeReducing out (some 1) kind
73added unless ms.size == 1 do
74added throwError m!"Failed to find {← ppExpr t} as the type of a parameter of {← ppExpr e}."
75added mvs := mvs ++ ms
76added bis := bis ++ bs
77added out := tp
78added return (mvs, bis, out)
79added
80added/-- Get the user-facing name for the given metavariable. -/
81addeddef _root_.Lean.MVarId.getUserName (mvarId : MVarId) : MetaM Name := do
82added let decl ← mvarId.getDecl
83added return decl.userName
84added
85added/-- Given equations `eqs` in the local context of `mvarId`,
86added unify them using [Lean.Meta.unifyEq?],
87added but if unification fails, leave the equation in the context.
88added This means we should never get a "Dependent elimination failed" error.
89added While marked partial, this _should_ always terminate,
90added decreasing on the sum of the sizes of the terms of each equation.
91added
92added Lifted from [Lean.Meta.Cases.unifyEqs]. -/
93addedpartial def unifyEqs (eqs : List FVarId) (mvarId : MVarId) (subst : FVarSubst) (caseName? : Option Name) : MetaM (MVarId × FVarSubst) := withIncRecDepth do
94added match eqs with
95added | [] => return (mvarId, subst)
96added | eq :: eqs =>
97added let some { mvarId, subst, numNewEqs } ← Option.join <$> (observing? $ unifyEq? mvarId eq subst MVarId.acyclic caseName?)
98added | unifyEqs eqs mvarId subst caseName?
99added let (newEqs, mvarId) ← mvarId.introN numNewEqs
100added let eqs := eqs.map (Expr.fvarId! ∘ subst.get)
101added unifyEqs (newEqs.toList ++ eqs) mvarId subst caseName?
102added
103added/-- Lifted from [Lean.Meta.Cases.unifyCasesEqs]. -/
104addeddef unifyCasesEqs (eqs : List FVarId) (subgoals : Array CasesSubgoal) : MetaM (Array CasesSubgoal) :=
105added subgoals.filterMapM fun s => do
106added let eqs := eqs.filterMap (Expr.fvarId? ∘ s.subst.get)
107added let (mvarId, subst) ← unifyEqs eqs s.mvarId s.subst s.ctorName
108added if (← mvarId.isAssignedOrDelayedAssigned) then return none
109added else return some { s with
110added mvarId := mvarId,
111added subst := subst,
112added fields := s.fields.map (subst.apply ·)
113added }
114added
115added/-- Try to clear the given fvars from the local context of each subgoal,
116added using the subgoals' substitution mappings to find the fvars.
117added
118added As with [MVarId.tryClearMany], the fvars must be in the order they appear in the context. -/
119addeddef casesClearMany (subgoals : Array CasesSubgoal) (fvarIds : Array FVarId) : MetaM (Array CasesSubgoal) :=
120added subgoals.mapM fun s => do
121added let fvarIds := fvarIds.filterMap (Expr.fvarId? ∘ s.subst.get)
122added let mvarId ← s.mvarId.tryClearMany fvarIds
123added return { s with mvarId }
124added
125addedend Lean.Meta

127addednamespace Lean.Elab.Tactic
128addedopen Meta Term
129added
130added-- [https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Tactic/Lemma.lean]
131added-- [https://github.com/leanprover-community/batteries/blob/main/Batteries/Tactic/Lemma.lean]
132added/-- Synonym for `theorem`. -/
133addedmacro "lemma " thm:declId sig:declSig val:declVal : command => `(theorem $thm $sig $val)
134added
135added/--
136added `apply t at i` uses forward reasoning with `t` at the hypothesis `i`.
137added Explicitly, if `t : α₁ → ⋯ → αᵢ → ⋯ → αₙ` and `i` has type `αᵢ`, then this tactic adds
138added metavariables/goals for any terms of `αⱼ` for `j = 1, …, i-1`,
139added then replaces the type of `i` with `αᵢ₊₁ → ⋯ → αₙ` by applying those metavariables and the
140added original `i`.
141added
142added Lifted from [https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Tactic/ApplyAt.lean].
143added-/
144addedelab "apply " t:term " at " i:ident : tactic => withSynthesize <| withMainContext do
145added let f ← elabTermForApply t
146added let some ldecl := (← getLCtx).findFromUserName? i.getId
147added | throwErrorAt i m!"Identifier {i} not found"
148added let (mvs, bis, _) ← forallMetaTelescopeReducingUntilDefEq (← inferType f) ldecl.type
149added for (m, b) in mvs.zip bis do
150added if b.isInstImplicit && !(← m.mvarId!.isAssigned) then
151added try m.mvarId!.inferInstance
152added catch _ => continue
153added let (_, mainGoal) ← (← getMainGoal).note ldecl.userName
154added (← mkAppOptM' f (mvs.pop.push ldecl.toExpr |>.map some))
155added let mainGoal ← mainGoal.tryClear ldecl.fvarId
156added replaceMainGoal <| [mainGoal] ++ mvs.pop.toList.map (·.mvarId!)
157added
158addedstructure InversionConfig where
159added clear : Bool := false
160added
161addeddeclare_config_elab elabInversionConfig InversionConfig
162added
163addedopen Cases in
164addeddef inversionCore (h : FVarId) (config : InversionConfig) : TacticM (List CasesSubgoal) := withMainContext do
165added let goal ← getMainGoal
166added goal.withContext do
167added let some ctx ← mkCasesContext? h
168added | throwTacticEx `inversion goal "Target {Expr.fvar h} does not belong to an inductive type"
169added -- If the target's type isn't a predicate with indices, behave like `cases`
170added if ← hasIndepIndices ctx then
171added let subgoals ← inductionCasesOn goal h default ctx
172added let subgoals ← if config.clear
173added then casesClearMany subgoals #[h]
174added else pure subgoals
175added return subgoals.toList
176added -- Otherwise, use custom [unifyEqs] to not fail on unifying HEqs
177added else
178added let gis@⟨newGoal, _, newTarget, numEqs⟩ ← generalizeIndices goal h
179added let (newEqs, newGoal) ← newGoal.introN numEqs
180added let some targetEq := newEqs.back?
181added | throwTacticEx `inversion newGoal "Failed to generalize target"
182added let subgoals ← inductionCasesOn newGoal newTarget default ctx
183added let subgoals ← elimAuxIndices gis subgoals
184added let subgoals ← unifyCasesEqs newEqs.toList subgoals
185added let subgoals ← if config.clear
186added then casesClearMany subgoals #[h, targetEq]
187added else pure subgoals
188added return subgoals.toList
189added
190added/-- Given an inversion alternative and a list of goals,
191added solve the tagged goal with the provided tactics,
192added throwing an error if the goal cannot be found or solved. -/
193addeddef evalInvAlt (goals : List CasesSubgoal) (alt : TSyntax `invAlt) : TacticM (List MVarId) :=
194added match alt with
195added | `(invAlt| | $tag:ident $vars:binderIdent* => $tactics:tacticSeq) => do
196added if let some goal := goals.find? (matchTag tag.getId $ ·.ctorName.getD default) then
197added return [← trySolveGoal vars tactics goal.mvarId]
198added else throwError m!"Invalid alternative name `{tag.getId}`: {← errorMsg}"
199added | `(invAlt| | _ $vars:binderIdent* => $tactics:tacticSeq) => do
200added if !goals.isEmpty then
201added goals.mapM (trySolveGoal vars tactics ·.mvarId)
202added else throwErrorAt alt m!"Invalid wildcard alternative: {← errorMsg}"
203added | _ => throwErrorAt alt "Could not parse inversion alternative"
204addedwhere
205added matchTag tag name : Bool :=
206added tag == name || tag.isPrefixOf name || tag.isSuffixOf name
207added trySolveGoal vars tactics goal : TacticM MVarId := do
208added let goals ← renameInaccessibles goal vars >>= evalTacticAt tactics
209added unless goals.isEmpty do
210added reportUnsolvedGoals goals
211added return goal
212added errorMsg : TacticM MessageData := do
213added let goalMsgs := goals.filterMap (.ofName <$> ·.ctorName)
214added return if goals.isEmpty
215added then m!"There are no unhandled alternatives"
216added else m!"Expected {.orList goalMsgs}"
217added
218added@[tactic Lean.Parser.inversion, inherit_doc Lean.Parser.inversion]
219addedpublic meta def evalInversion : Tactic
220added | `(tactic| inversion $config $h:ident $[with $[$alts?:invAlts]*]?) => do
221added let config ← elabInversionConfig config
222added let mut goals ← inversionCore (← getFVarId h) config
223added if let some alts := alts? then
224added let expandedAlts ← Array.flatten <$> alts.mapM expandInvAlts
225added for alt in expandedAlts do
226added let solvedGoals ← evalInvAlt goals alt
227added goals := goals.filter (!solvedGoals.contains ·.mvarId)
228added unless goals.isEmpty do
229added reportUnsolvedGoals $ goals.map (·.mvarId)
230added replaceMainGoal $ goals.map (·.mvarId)
231added | stx => throwErrorAt stx "Could not parse inversion tactic"
232addedwhere expandInvAlts
233added | `(invAlts| $[| $args:caseArg]* => $tactics:tacticSeq) =>
234added args.mapM (`(invAlt| | $(·) => $tactics))
235added | stx => throwErrorAt stx "Could not parse inversion alternatives"
236added
237addedend Lean.Elab.Tactic
238added
239addedend -- meta section
